sehemu: Part III: Procedure, Powers and Privileges of Parliament
maudhui: (1) There shall be a Speaker of the National Assembly who shall be elected by Members from among persons who are Members of Parliament or are qualified to be Members; he shall be the leader of the National Assembly and shall represent it in all other bodies and meetings outside Parliament. (2) A Minister, Deputy Minister or a person holding any other office prescribed by a law enacted by Parliament for purposes of this Article shall not be eligible for election as Speaker. (3) A person elected Speaker shall, within fifteen days of his election, submit to the President a formal declaration that he has not lost the qualifications for election in accordance with Article 67(2)(d). (4) The President shall submit to the Ethics Commissioner one copy of every formal declaration submitted to him under subarticle (3). (5) The Speaker shall submit to the President two copies of a formal statement containing particulars of his property and, where applicable, the property of his spouse. (6) The provisions of Article 70(2) and (3) shall apply, so far as practicable, to any statement of property made by the Speaker. (7) The Speaker shall cease to be Speaker and shall vacate the office upon the occurrence of any of the following: (a) if elected from among Members, he ceases to be a Member for any reason other than dissolution of Parliament; (b) any circumstance arises which, if he were not Speaker, would render him ineligible for election or cause him to lose qualification for election as Speaker; (c) Parliament first meets after a General Election following dissolution; (d) he is removed from office by a resolution of the National Assembly supported by not less than two-thirds of all Members; (e) he fails to submit the formal declaration to the President; (f) he is convicted of an offence of giving false information; (g) he fails to submit a statement of property to the President; or (h) it is established that he has contravened the law concerning the ethics of public leaders. (8) No business shall be transacted in the National Assembly, except the election of a Speaker, at any time when the office of Speaker is vacant. (9) A person who is not a Member of Parliament and is elected Speaker shall, before entering upon his functions, take and subscribe before the National Assembly the oath of allegiance.
